topic: Pure Fourier Series: Deconstructing the World into Waves

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Deconstructing the World into Waves

sections.title: The Grand Analogy: The Secret Recipe of Sound
sections.content: Introduce the core concept using a character: 'Echo the Bat.' Echo hears a complex sound but needs to understand its ingredients. Explain that any complex, repeating sound is just a 'soup' made of simple pure tones (sine and cosine waves). This sets the stage for decomposition.
sections.example: Visualize Echo the Bat looking at a messy 'Square Wave' sound and seeing it split into several colorful, smooth sine waves of different heights and speeds.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Building Blocks (Unit Circles)
sections.content: Briefly refresh the link between circular motion and trigonometry. Show how a point moving around a circle at a constant speed traces a sine wave over time. Establish the 'Period' (T) and 'Fundamental Frequency' as the base speed of our fastest building block.
sections.example: An animation of a wheel rolling forward, with a pen attached to the rim tracing a perfect red sine curve on a wall.

sections.title: The Fourier Formula: The Ingredient List
sections.content: Introduce the general Fourier Series equation: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ [aₙ cos(nωx) + bₙ sin(nωx)]. Explain that 'a₀' is the average height (DC offset), while 'aₙ' and 'bₙ' are the volumes (amplitudes) of the specific cosine and sine ingredients.
sections.example: A 'Mixing Console' graphic where sliding the 'a₁' fader makes the first wave taller, and changing 'n' adds faster, zig-zagging waves to the mix.

sections.title: Orthogonality: How to Pick the Ingredients
sections.content: Explain the 'magic' of how we find the coefficients. Use the concept of 'Mathematical Filtering' (Orthogonality). If you multiply a signal by a specific sine wave and integrate over one period, only the matching ingredient survives; the rest cancel out to zero.
sections.example: A visual 'Sieve' or 'Filter' where a complex wave passes through a blue sine-shaped hole. Only the blue parts of the original wave get through to be measured.

sections.title: Case Study: Assembling the Square Wave
sections.content: Demonstrate the step-by-step construction of a Square Wave using only odd-numbered sine waves. Show how adding the 1st, 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics gradually transforms a smooth curve into a sharp, boxy shape (Gibbs Phenomenon).
sections.example: A 'Wave-Builder' machine where a character adds 1/3 sin(3x), then 1/5 sin(5x). Graphically show the 'ripples' at the corners of the square wave getting tighter as more terms are added.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Echoes
sections.content: Summarize that the Fourier Series is a bridge between the 'Time Domain' (what we see) and the 'Frequency Domain' (the recipe). Mention applications like MP3 compression or image processing.
sections.example: Show a smartphone 'Spectrum Analyzer' app vibrating as Echo the Bat chirps, turning the sound into a bar graph of frequencies.

storyboard.title: The Grand Analogy: The Secret Recipe of Sound
lecture_lines: Complex sounds are like recipes made of simple ingredients.
Meet Echo the Bat, hearing a complex square wave.
Every repeating wave is just a sum of pure tones.
animations: Fade in Echo the Bat (using simple shapes) at #FFFFFF.
Create a jagged 'Square Wave' in #00FFFF across the screen.
Transform the square wave into a collection of sine waves.
Separate the sine waves vertically, assigning colors #FF0000, #00FF00, and #0000FF.
Scale the sine waves to show different amplitudes and frequencies.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Building Blocks (Unit Circles)
lecture_lines: Circular motion naturally creates smooth sine and cosine waves.
A point rotating at constant speed traces a wave.
The fundamental frequency sets the base speed of motion.
animations: Draw a circle #FFFFFF and a point rotating on its edge.
Trace a red (#FF0000) sine curve as the point rotates.
Label the horizontal distance for one cycle as 'Period (T)'.

storyboard.title: The Fourier Formula: The Ingredient List
lecture_lines: The Fourier Series formula represents periodic functions mathematically.
Constant a-zero represents the average value or DC offset.
Coefficients a-n and b-n control the amplitude of waves.
Higher frequencies add more detail to the complex signal.
Together, they reconstruct the original function perfectly.
animations: Display formula: f(x) = a0/2 + sum(...) in #FFFFFF.
Shift the entire wave vertically to highlight the a0/2 offset.
Add a second, faster sine wave (#00FF00) to the original wave.
Flash an and bn while scaling the wave amplitudes.
Show a mixing fader moving up, increasing a wave's height.

storyboard.title: Orthogonality: How to Pick the Ingredients
lecture_lines: Orthogonality acts as a mathematical filter for specific frequencies.
Multiply the signal by a target sine or cosine.
Integrating over one period cancels out non-matching waves.
Only the component matching the filter's frequency remains.
This process isolates every individual ingredient in the recipe.
animations: Show a complex wave (#00FFFF) and a pure sine wave (#FF00FF).
Visualize the two waves multiplying, resulting in a new wave.
Fill the area under the product wave; highlight it in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Case Study: Assembling the Square Wave
lecture_lines: Let's build a square wave using only odd harmonics.
Start with the fundamental sine wave at base frequency.
Add the third harmonic at one-third of the amplitude.
Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the shape.
Ripples at the edges are known as Gibbs Phenomenon.
animations: Plot sin(x) in #FF0000.
Add (1/3)sin(3x) in #00FF00; show the sum wave flattening.
Add (1/5)sin(5x) in #0000FF; the sum wave becomes more square.
Continue adding higher harmonics until a box shape forms.
Highlight the overshoot at the corners in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Summary & Real-World Echoes
lecture_lines: Fourier Series bridges the time and frequency domains.
Complex signals become simple lists of frequency components.
These recipes power modern technology like digital audio compression.
animations: Show a wave morphing into a bar graph (spectrum analyzer).
Display a smartphone icon (#FFFFFF) with vibrating frequency bars.
Flash the words 'MP3' and 'JPEG' in #00FFFF.
